notes: Synthetic: from Mistral's official SDK, github.com/mistralai/client-python at 90e300904b64c36e0630f72ef475dbab7912068e (2026-10-28), whose models are generated by Speakeasy from Mistral's OpenAPI spec, POST /v1/audio/transcriptions as multipart (transcriptions.py, operation audio_api_v1_transcriptions_post): AudioTranscriptionRequest (model, file, language, ...) and the 200, application/json TranscriptionResponse {model, text, usage UsageInfo, language, segments (only with timestamp_granularities)}. The model is the SDK's transcription examples' (examples/mistral/audio/transcription_segments.py); the text is what the upload says, and the usage values are placeholders of UsageInfo's shape. The adapter lifts text and passes the body through. The stream variant (transcriptions#stream) is not driven: models.TranscriptionRequest has no stream field. error_invalid_model is the error body of the SDK's test_error_response (extra/tests/test_otel_tracing.py) verbatim, status 400 as there: the API error body the SDK's error hook reads (extra/observability/otel.py), gap MI1. The operation types no other 4XX body. Mistral's spec itself (Speakeasy registry, docs.mistral.ai) was not reachable from the authoring sandbox.

allowed_unknown_fields.reason: no canonical field: the body is passed through to the client unchanged (TranscriptionResponse.Body); the gateway reads text alone

known gap O18: the upstream usage is ignored; the server prices transcription and translation from the uploaded WAV's duration (server/handlers_audio.go), so token-billed gpt-4o-*-transcribe models are priced by the wrong unit and non-WAV uploads go unpriced. Mistral's usage carries prompt_audio_seconds, the duration it bills; the body still reaches the client unchanged

known gap MI1: Mistral's error body is {"object": "error", "message", "type", "param", "code"} at the top level, not OpenAI's {"error": {...}}; parseProviderError finds no error.message and falls back to a 502 with the raw body as the message, so a 400 or 401 is retried, failed over and counted against the circuit breaker
